validity.recommendation: Do not 'fix' LengthKnownKm to the measured 608 km schematic draw — per protocol gotcha 3 that requires the draw to FAR exceed the stated value (this country's two named exceptions are P0784 and P1481, not this row), and a length correction with no citable source would violate the no-fabrication rule regardless. Instead flag LengthKnownKm=297.00 as SCOPE-PARTIAL: two independent sources show this corridor was built in two documented stages three years apart (1982 to Kursk/under the 'Yelets-Kursk-Kyiv' name, 1985 Kursk-to-Kyiv as a separately named build), so 297.00 most plausibly measures only the first-stage segment, not the full corridor the row's own PipelineName and endpoints describe. A human should decide whether to (a) leave LengthKnownKm as-is with a ResearcherNotes caveat that it likely undercounts the full corridor pending a source that states the 1985 extension's own length, or (b) research the Kursk-Kyiv 1985 extension specifically (Sumy Oblast/Poltava/Kyiv Oblast regional gas-supply archives, on the same e-gorod.ru pattern I used for Kursk/Lipetsk, would be the next rung — I did not have time to pull the Sumy/Poltava/Kyiv oblast equivalents in this pass). Either way, do not touch StartYear1 (1981, close to the chronology's 1982) — that is not this brief's flag.
validity.researcher_notes: This brief's only flagged question for P0776 is length_ratio (608 km drawn vs 297.00 km stated); the redundancy leg's existence/duplicate verdict and the staged Gazprom-ownership-attribution concern (48.6%/100% on these two rows) are both already settled/escalated elsewhere and I have not restated or re-litigated them. Two findings, the second of which is decisive: (1) Ukrtransgaz's own official corporate chronology (utg.ua, reached via Wayback because the live site 403s per gotcha 1) lists TWO separate commissioning entries for this corridor, three years apart: '1982 р. Введено в експлуатацію магістральний газопровід Єлець - Курськ – Київ' ('In 1982, the Yelets-Kursk-Kyiv trunk gas pipeline was commissioned') and, distinctly, '1985 р. Введено в експлуатацію Сумську КС; введено в експлуатацію магістральний газопровід Курськ - Київ' ('In 1985, the Sumy compressor station was commissioned; [and] the Kursk-Kyiv trunk gas pipeline was commissioned') — note the second entry drops the 'Yelets-' prefix and is its own named build, with its own compressor station (Sumy) added at the same time. This is the same document the source_ladder expected to close the ownership cluster; it also directly answers the length question by showing the corridor to Kyiv was NOT one project. (2) Independent corroboration of that same shape, from a completely different origin: eegas.com (East European Gas Analysis, M. Korchemkin's technical table of Ukraine's import/export pipelines, verified live) lists 'Yelets-Kursk-Dikan'ka (Sudzha)' at 15 bcm/yr as one line, and separately 'Kursk-Kiev (Sudzha)' — again dropping 'Yelets-' — at 14 bcm/yr, both entering Ukraine at the same Sudzha crossing. An independent technical-press source using the identical 'Kursk-Kiev' (not 'Yelets-Kursk-Kiev') naming as Ukrtransgaz's own 1985 chronology entry corroborates that the Kursk-to-Kyiv leg is treated, in both sources, as its own segment layered onto the earlier, shared Yelets-Kursk trunk — the same trunk P0775 (Dykanka) also descends from. That materially changes the reading of the length_ratio flag: 297.00 km is not simply 'wrong' against the 608 km drawn span, it most likely counts only the 1982-vintage Yelets-Kursk segment (which is why it sits almost exactly at P0775's 298.00 km — a physically shorter corridor that WAS built as one project — despite this row's true corridor to Kyiv, including the 1985 Kursk-Kyiv extension via Sumy, Hrebinka and Glushkove compressor stations per Ukrainian Wikipedia's station list for this line, being considerably longer than the Dykanka corridor). (3) Struck out: energybase.ru (cited on gem.wiki for this row) IP-blocks this environment and is robots-excluded from the Wayback Machine (confirmed via CDX 'excluded' notice), so I could not check it as GEM's possible length origin. Kursk and Lipetsk oblasts' official 2001 gas-supply-system documents (e-gorod.ru, via Wayback) give only oblast-wide aggregate mileage, never a per-pipeline breakdown. I did not locate a source giving the 1985 Kursk-Kyiv extension's own length, so the FULL corridor length for this row remains unresolved even though the SCOPE of the existing 297.00 figure is now well explained.
